COSTING & FINANCING

What makes a programme financeable?

A useful investment case connects costs, funding, implementation and the assumptions that hold them together.

PRACTICE GUIDE
3 MIN READ
01

Start with the decision

Define who needs to decide what, by when, and which alternatives remain open. A model should serve that decision.

02

Separate cost from funding

Identify capital, operating and lifecycle costs. Then ask which funding sources can credibly cover them, on what terms and when.

03

Expose the assumptions

Make the key drivers visible: uptake, delivery pace, unit costs, financing terms and maintenance. Use sensitivity analysis to understand which assumptions change the choice.

04

Cost the implementation system

Include the capacity, procurement, governance, monitoring and ongoing operations needed to make the programme work.

05

Make the financing gap explicit

Show what is funded, what is conditional and what remains unresolved. A clear gap is more useful than an apparently balanced plan built on optimistic assumptions.
